summary:
Third candidate (action=obligation) on an authority-transition gap, plus a map extension; preflight-validated with valid=True and no diagnostics.

Sourced discrepancy: the TimeoutNow receive handler validates nothing beyond the RPC-header version window. TimeoutNowRequest carries only an RPCHeader, so no term is available for a currency check (commands.go:204-218); processRPC applies only the version gate before dispatch (raft.go:1396-1412); and timeoutNow then clears the known leader, sets the node to Candidate and raises candidateFromLeadershipTransfer, responding success unconditionally (raft.go:2208-2214). That flag is the code's own 'abusable' privilege: runCandidate skips the pre-vote campaign and sends RequestVote with LeadershipTransfer=true, which peers grant despite already having a leader (raft.go:284-307 and requestVote). By contrast, requestVote and requestPreVote both reject senders that are not in the receiver's configuration, and leadership votes are granted only when the privilege is set.

Product contents: obligation claim-timeout-now-attribution (implementation_semantics) — a TimeoutNow request is honoured only when its sender is attributed to the receiver's authority context, at minimum a voter of the receiver's latest configuration; one question grounded on the new principal Fact f-leader-transfer-privilege (A2), direct Behavior b-timeout-now (A2), lifecycle establishment, with supporting behaviors b-vote-campaign, b-vote-grant and b-leadership-transfer; and one physical binding (symbol timeoutNow, raft.go:2209-2214).

Map extension (base version 7): new Behavior b-timeout-now, new Fact f-leader-transfer-privilege, and a new consumer edge on b-vote-campaign; no accepted object's meaning, identity or existing edges changed, so the two confirmed findings keep their original basis.

Retained counterevidence and unknowns, not suppressed: the version window still applies, only a leader normally sends TimeoutNow so the handler may rely on leader discipline, the missing term check may be a design consequence rather than oversight, and the LeadershipTransfer API doc presents mixed-cluster transfers as safe. Reachability by a non-member sender, the effect on a healthy leader, and whether the design intends to trust leader discipline are the explicit premises a later check must resolve. No violation is asserted yet.
